Up to $2 million in grant money for AI that fixes city services, and round 1 closes in 9 days.

Cities Deliver is a $50 million global grant programme from The Rockefeller Foundation and the OpenAI Foundation. It funds teams that work with a city government to deploy AI that improves public services for underserved residents in public health, economic mobility, environmental resilience or civic services.

There are two tracks. The seed track gives $500,000 to under $1 million for early concepts ready for a first city pilot, and the scale track gives $1 million to $2 million for solutions already piloted with early results. Grants run for 24 months, half paid upfront and half after a mid-term milestone, and no equity is taken.

Indian non-profits, university labs and public benefit companies can lead, and for-profit startups can apply in limited cases if the project is charitable, open-source in approach and the grant money is ring-fenced.

The catch most founders miss: you need a letter of intent from a city partner with 50,000+ residents and its own municipal government. That letter is the real bottleneck, so start that conversation today.

Last date: 29 November 2026

Running a business with ₹30 lakh+ turnover? Goldman Sachs will pay for your IIM growth programme.

Goldman Sachs 10,000 Women India is a free executive-education programme for established women business owners, taught by faculty from IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Bangalore and IIM Lucknow. It covers finance, marketing, negotiation and leadership across three in-person residential modules and more than 100 hours of learning.

Tuition is fully paid by Goldman Sachs. You also get business mentoring from industry experts and a place in an alumnae network of over 4,000 Indian women business owners, plus the global 10,000 Women community. No equity is involved.

You can apply if you are the woman owner or co-owner and the main decision-maker, your business has run for at least a year, turns over roughly ₹30 lakh or more a year and has at least three employees. Every industry is welcome, but past graduates cannot reapply.

One thing to plan for: travel and lodging for the residential weeks are not covered, and this is not a cash grant. The first step is only a 2-minute expression-of-interest form, so there is no reason to wait.

Last date: 30 November 2026

No co-founder. No idea. Still want to build a startup? This is the programme designed for exactly that.

Entrepreneur First runs a 14-week programme in Bangalore that recruits individuals, not companies. You join a cohort of technical and commercial builders, find a co-founder, shape an idea together, and pitch EF for investment. The Winter 2027 cohort starts in February 2027, and 1 December is the cut-off for its third selection round.

Teams EF chooses to back receive pre-seed money of up to $250,000. The reported standard deal is $125,000 on a post-money SAFE for 8%, with an optional further $125,000 on an uncapped MFN SAFE. Funded teams then spend three more months in San Francisco and get access to EF's global investor and alumni network.

It suits early-career people with standout results compared to their peers who can commit full-time and in person in Bangalore. Existing co-founders can apply, but each should submit a separate application.

The catch: this is equity, not a grant, and only backed teams get money. Funded companies are expected to move to San Francisco, and EF may help with visas but does not provide them.

Last date: 1 December 2026
